For an initial value problem y′=f(x,y),y(a)=c, the increment in y using the Runge-Kutta Method with step size Δx is computed as the weighted average of four sample slopes: Δy=16(y′+2y1′+2y2′+y3′)⋅Δx, where

  • y′=f(x,y) is the slope at the initial point (x,y),

  • y1′=f(x1,y1) is the slope at (x1,y1)=(x+12Δx,y+12y′⋅Δx),

  • y2′=f(x2,y2) is the slope at (x2,y2)=(x+12Δx,y+12y1′⋅Δx),

  • y3′=f(x3,y3) is the slope at (x3,y3)=(x+Δx,y+y2′⋅Δx).

Now let's find the required values.

  • First, we compute the value of y′ according to the given rule: y′=2x−4y=2⋅1−4⋅12=2−2=0. So, we add this to our table.

    x y y′ y1′ y2′ y3′ Δy
    1 12 0

  • The first intermediate point is (x1,y1)=(x+12Δx,y+12y′⋅Δx)=(1+12⋅14,12+12⋅0⋅14)=(98,12). So, the first intermediate slope is y1′=2x1−4y1=2⋅98−4⋅12=14. We can add this to our table.

    x y y′ y1′ y2′ y3′ Δy
    1 12 0 14

  • The second intermediate point is (x2,y2)=(x+12Δx,y+12y1′⋅Δx)=(1+12⋅14,12+12⋅14⋅14)=(98,1732). So, the second intermediate slope is y2′=2x2−4y2=2⋅98−4⋅1732=18. We add this to our table.

    x y y′ y1′ y2′ y3′ Δy
    1 12 0 14 18

  • The third intermediate point is (x3,y3)=(x+Δx,y+y2′⋅Δx)=(1+14,12+18⋅14)=(54,1732). So, the third intermediate slope is y3′=2x3−4y3=2⋅54−4⋅1732=38. We can add this to our table.

    x y y′ y1′ y2′ y3′ Δy
    1 12 0 14 18 38

Finally, we compute Δy using the Runge-Kutta Method:

Δy=16(y′+2y1′+2y2′+y3′)⋅Δx=16(0+2⋅14+2⋅18+38)⋅14=124⋅98=364.

Therefore, the completed first row is as given below.

x y y′ y1′ y2′ y3′ Δy
1 12 0 14 18 38 364

To get the values of x and y in the next row, we add Δx to x and Δy to y, as follows:

xnew=x+Δx=1+14=54ynew=y+Δy=12+364=3564

Adding these rows to our table gives the following:

x y y′ y1′ y2′ y3′ Δy
1 12 0 14 18 38 364
54 3564

Finally, we have

y(54)≈3564.
